question.worked_solution:
First, we use the definition of the biconditional statement to write the equivalence as a conjunction of implications: 

$$
¬(P⇔Q)≡¬((P⇒Q)∧(Q⇒P))
$$

Now, we represent all the implications using disjunctions and negations:

$$
¬((P⇒Q)∧(Q⇒P))≡¬((¬P∨Q)∧(¬Q∨P))
$$

Next, we use De Morgan's laws:

$$
\begin{aligned}¬((¬P∨Q)∧(¬Q∨P)) & ≡¬(¬P∨Q)∨¬(¬Q∨P) \\  & ≡(¬¬P∧¬Q)∨(¬¬Q∧¬P)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we simplify the double negations and write down symbols in alphabetic order inside the parentheses using commutative laws:

$$
\begin{aligned}(¬¬P∧¬Q)∨(¬¬Q∧¬P)≡(P∧¬Q)∨(Q∧¬P) \\ ≡(P∧¬Q)∨(¬P∧Q)\end{aligned}
$$
